11 A stone is projected horizontally in a vacuum and moves along the path shown.
path of stone
H
X
T
V
X is a point on this path. XV and XH are vertical and horizontal lines respectively through X. XT is
the tangent to the path at X.
Along which directions do forces act on the stone at X?
A
XV and XH
B
XV only
C
XH only
D
XT only

hints: Notice the stone is in a vacuum, so think about whether air resistance can act along XH or opposite to XT.
Recall that a horizontally projected object still has only one interaction with the Earth after launch.
Compare the directions XV, XH and XT with the direction of weight $W = mg$ at point X.
walkthrough: Identify the situation at X: the stone is already in flight, projected horizontally and moving in a vacuum along a curved path.
List possible forces: weight due to gravity, plus any contact forces or air resistance. Once projected there is no contact, and vacuum means no air resistance or drag.
State the governing rule: by Newton's laws the only remaining force is weight $W = mg$ acting vertically downwards towards the Earth.
Compare this with the marked lines: XV is the vertical line through X, XH is horizontal, and XT is the tangent along the velocity.
Therefore the single force aligns with XV only, with no component along XH or along XT. This is option B.

A.explanation: There is no horizontal force in a vacuum, so no component acts along XH.

B.explanation: In a vacuum there is no air resistance, so the only force is weight acting vertically down along XV.

C.explanation: Horizontal velocity needs no horizontal force to continue, so no force acts along XH.

D.explanation: XT is the direction of velocity at X, but force is not in the direction of motion for a projectile.
